rationale: BLOCKED, leaning YES. I read the complete held EO 13899 (84 FR 68779, Dec. 11, 2019, Combating Anti-Semitism): sec. 1 policy to enforce Title VI against anti-Semitic discrimination; sec. 2 directs agencies enforcing Title VI to consider the IHRA working definition and examples; sec. 3 requires agency reports within 120 days (a one-time report deadline, not a status basis); sec. 4 rule of construction; sec. 5 general provisions. It has no sunset and no savings clause. The only history observation is the catalog note 'See: EO 14188, January 29, 2025'. I read the passages of the held EO 14188 that mention EO 13899: the preamble states that EO 14188 'reaffirms Executive Order 13899' and says the prior administration 'effectively nullified' it by failing to enforce it, and the order directs further agency measures. That is a reaffirmation, not a revocation or supersession, and it is not an operative amendment I can identify in the held excerpts, so the cross-reference does not end 13899. The history therefore supports no NO; the remaining question is whether it is still in effect through 2026-10-14, which needs a held current predicate (a printed U.S. Code note or Federal Register current-status record) that is not available. The U.S. Code lead prints the order with no ending statement but is a pointer only.
